paper.title: Ace-Skill: Bootstrapping Multimodal Agents with Prioritized and Clustered Evolution
paper.central_claim: Jointly optimizing rollout allocation (a prioritized sampler with lazy-decay proficiency tracking) and knowledge organization (cluster-isolated tactical-experience and strategic-skill pools) breaks a self-reinforcing 'data inefficiency / knowledge interference' loop, giving +35.46% relative Avg@4 over vanilla tool use, letting a 35B MoE match or beat proprietary models, and transferring zero-shot to 9B/4B models.

signatures.object: Rollout-allocation schedule over the bootstrapping pool (per-sample proficiency state v_i with lazy-decayed Beta posterior); baseline = sequential/uniform traversal.
signatures.information: Scalar reward r in [0,1] from an LLM verifier (same MLLM; ground-truth answers are part of the training pool); no test labels at inference.
signatures.operation: Update decayed (alpha, beta) per revisited sample -> weight = sqrt(v(1-v)) + gamma(1-v) + eps -> draw batch of 8.
signatures.output: Next batch of samples for rollout and distillation.
signatures.conditions: rho=0.95, gamma=0.4, eps=0.1, 50 steps, 1 rollout per sample.
signatures.selection_rule: Stochastic priority sampling (uncertainty + hardness + exploration floor).
signatures.selection_data: The same pool the memory is built from; whether it overlaps the evaluated benchmark samples is not stated.
signatures.persistence: Proficiency vector exists only during bootstrapping; the persisted result is the memory it fed.
signatures.later_use: Controls which trajectories get distilled into the memory.
signatures.claimed_effect: Sampler alone: TIR-Bench Avg@4 39.37 -> 46.25; >30% of samples visited >4 times and >39% <4 times over 4 epochs.
signatures.failure_boundary: Excess difficulty bias hurts coverage (Fig 5); no learning-curve vs uniform at equal rollouts; single-rollout reward is noisy.

signatures.object: Cluster-isolated knowledge memory: per cluster a tactical experience pool (<=120 entries, similarity-merge threshold 0.70) and a strategic skill document (<= about 1000 words); baseline = single global pool as in XSkill.
signatures.information: Trajectory + verifier reward; distillation by the same MLLM; cluster routing from text embedding of the task description (K-means, fixed a priori).
signatures.operation: Distill delta experience and delta skill after each rollout -> route to the sample's cluster -> insert or LLM-merge by similarity -> compact/compress to caps.
signatures.conditions: K (cluster count) not reported; clusters fixed; skill document rewritten per rollout.
signatures.selection_rule: Similarity threshold and capacity compaction; no test of whether an entry helps, no retirement by utility, no rollback or versioning.
signatures.persistence: Memory frozen after bootstrapping and injected at test time.
signatures.later_use: At test time the task is routed to its cluster; top-k cosine experiences and the full skill document (adapted per task) are concatenated into the prompt; also injected into 9B/4B models and into other benchmarks.
signatures.claimed_effect: Mean Avg@4 31.40 vs 23.18 (vanilla tools) and 25.87 (XSkill); organizer alone 45.75 vs 39.37 on TIR-Bench; zero-shot transfer to 9B/4B and OOD benchmarks.
signatures.failure_boundary: Cross-type noise in global pool (single case study); on 122B removing the experience cluster costs only 0.12 points.

gap.author_gap: Self-evolving agents (a) spend rollout budget on low-value samples (data inefficiency) and (b) mix heterogeneous knowledge in one global pool (knowledge interference), which interact in a self-reinforcing loop.
gap.checked_gap: Both are plausible, specific shortcomings of prior experience/skill bootstrapping (global pool, uniform traversal), supported by a case study and ablations. The coupling loop and the claim that most prior work uses a single granularity are only partly checked: XSkill, the closest neighbour, already keeps experiences and skills.
gap.lineage: Reflexion -> ExpeL-style experience pools -> XSkill (dual-stream experiences + skills in one global pool) -> Memento-Skills / Trace2Skill / SkillX / SkillRouter; RL-based D2Skill/SkillRL form a separate weight-updating family. Ace-Skill = XSkill-style memory + per-cluster isolation + proficiency-prioritized rollouts.
gap.closest_adjacent: XSkill (compared experimentally on same backbone); SkillRouter (routing over a large registry), D2Skill (dual-granularity skill bank with RL) are named but not compared.
gap.residue: Whether clustering beats other organisations (hierarchy/graph/router) and whether the sampler reduces cost at fixed rollouts; K sensitivity; train/test overlap.
gap.stakes: Rollout/verification cost in long-horizon multimodal tool use and retrieval noise as task diversity grows.
gap.method_response: Prioritized sampler for allocation; clustered dual-granularity organizer for isolation; claimed mutual reinforcement.
gap.remaining_gap: Admission gate and retirement of stored knowledge, independent verifier, open-ended cluster discovery, cost accounting.
unresolved: Neighbour full texts (XSkill, SkillRouter, D2Skill) not fixed in this batch, so gap check relies on the paper's characterisation and Table 2 numbers.

claims.text: Ace-Skill improves Qwen3.5-35B-A3B tool use by +35.46% relative Avg@4 (mean 23.18 -> 31.40) and beats XSkill (25.87) and several proprietary models.

claims.allowed_conclusion: On these benchmarks the system with its bootstrapped memory scores higher than the stated baselines (author-reported); generalisation to unseen samples of the same benchmark is not established.

M.reason: Both seats 3; re-checked. The Beta posterior with lazy decay, the three-term priority, and cluster-local dual-granularity memory with merge/compress are reproducible and give testable predictions against uniform sampling and a global pool. X.reason: Opus sides with son55. Algorithm 1 and Eqs. 3–8 describe the loop, but the conditions needed to reproduce it are missing. The number of clusters K and what text is embedded for clustering are not stated. The relation of the bootstrapping pool to the evaluation items is not stated (opus:O01). Whether the same-model verifier uses the ground-truth answer is not stated. There is no admission gate, utility-based retirement, versioning or rollback. The skill document is rewritten whole on every merge, and the Beta initialisation differs between text (0.5, 0.5) and Algorithm 1 (0) (sol's finding).

E.measurement.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. Four established benchmarks with Avg@4/Pass@4, but the scoring/judging procedure is not described, sourced and reproduced baseline numbers are mixed, and Ace-Skill runs in no-thinking mode while the baselines' modes are unstated.

E.causality.reason: Both seats 2; re-checked. A store-off arm (Vanilla Tools), XSkill on the same backbone, a 2×2 module ablation and component removals. Gaps: ablations on TIR-Bench only and single-run; no budget parity with XSkill and no simple context baseline. The 'super-additive' claim is contradicted by the paper's own numbers: +6.88 and +6.38 alone vs +10.63 combined.

E.holdout.reason: Opus sides with son55. Figure 3 shows the sampler visiting each benchmark's own samples (about 100 per pool, opus:O01), and the text never states that these are disjoint from the items behind Table 2. ρ/γ were tuned on TIR-Bench results and adopted 'in all other experiments' (opus:O02). Only the two cross-benchmark OOD pairs are clearly held out, and one target (TIR-Bench) is the tuning benchmark. Cross-model transfer reuses the same benchmarks. Main held-out status cannot be credited (EVIDENCE rule 2), so 1 rather than 2.

E.statistics.reason: Both seats 1 (A2 tier 1): Avg@4 over four attempts and Pass@4, but no benchmark sizes, seeds across bootstrapping runs, intervals or tests; ablation margins are 1–3 points.

E.cost.reason: Both seats 1; re-checked. The bootstrapping budget is given in natural units (400 single rollouts of ≤10/20 turns, 8×H20). Token, time or dollar cost is not given.
